clue.text: "12 ______" (The 27) — "Is 14 11" and "Shleps his wet feet" his translation

definitions.note: with the linked answers filled in, this reads as being finished, beyond all hope

indicators.note: a translation turns the words into another form, so the letters of the quoted phrase plus the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mob movie's famous line about its enforcer is set beside a Yiddish-flavoured rendering about trudging with soggy feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening part sets the scene: in The Godfather (27) it is said of Luca Brasi (12) after his murder. The anagram uses every letter of 'Shleps his wet feet' together with the second 'his'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia idiom means someone has been killed and dumped in the sea, so is dead and finished, like a doomed plan.

clue.text: Drink around eight, get tight and flop

indicators.note: the word for drink goes around the rowing team, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink around eight o'clock, gets drunk and collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get tight' is surface colour and a nod to the answer's other sense of screwing something tight. An eight in rowing is a boat's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-up is a blunder or failure, much as a flop is an enterprise that fails.

clue.text: Power held by eco-model, the centre of Disney's future

indicators.note: the power letter is held inside the eco piece, so one sits within the other

parts.note: taken as written from the clue's eco-
P is the physics abbreviation for power
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded design embodies energy, at the heart of Disney's plans for tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because the Florida park's name stands for Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow: a Disney centre about the future.
explanation.definitionFit: The Walt Disney World park was conceived as a showcase community of tomorrow, a Disney site devoted to the future.

clue.text: Trouble with teeth: bad or ropey? Ah!

indicators.note: bad letters are spoilt, so these words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dentist's patient groans over a mouth that looks bad or ropey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like part of the patient's description but signals the anagram of OR ROPEY AH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gum disease with discharge of pus, causing loosening of the teeth: dental trouble.

clue.text: See 1
Such strikers angry hearing Clause Four activist?

parts.note: wild means furious or angry
'Clause' heard aloud is claws, and the animal on all four legs that puts its claws to work is a cat

explanation.surface: Union members out on strike are furious, as one might expect of a left-winger loyal to Labour's Clause Four.
explanation.walkthrough: Clause Four was the old Labour Party commitment to public ownership, beloved of militants. Heard aloud it becomes claws on four paws, which leads to the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildcat strike is an unofficial walkout, so its strikers are wildcat strikers.

clue.text: Rule of this from a practised hand?

definitions.text: Rule of this from a practised hand?

parts.words: Rule of this from a practised hand?
parts.note: a practical rule of guidance based on experience is called a rule of this part of the hand

explanation.walkthrough: The 'rule of' phrase is completed by the answer: a rough working principle learned by experience, the sort a practised hand uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiomatic guideline from experience is named after this digit of the hand, hence the reference to a practised hand.

clue.text: Inaction's disturbed the maestro

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order, so Inaction's is rearranged

parts.note: read as 'inaction is', keeping the S as a letter

explanation.surface: A conductor is upset by the idleness of his orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Inaction's' counts, read as 'Inaction is disturbed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was the celebrated Italian conductor, a maestro in the musical sense.

clue.text: Involve leave with restrictions

definitions.meaning: to necessitate or involve as a consequence
to bequeath property so that it passes only to a set line of heirs

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to involve a consequence and to settle an estate on a restricted line of heirs.

clue.text: He'll tak ye tae the quarry

definitions.text: He'll tak ye tae the quarry

parts.words: He'll tak ye tae the quarry
parts.note: in Scots dialect: a man who guides sportsmen to the game they hunt or fish for

explanation.walkthrough: The quarry is not a stone pit but the hunted animal; the Scots spelling hints at the Highland estate attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland attendant who guides shooting and fishing parties leads them to their quarry, the game.

clue.text: Trojan 'ero in retreat returned like Stephen Fry at Dundee

indicators.note: the hero sits inside the turned hideaway, one piece within the other
the word for retreat is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's retreat or den
the Trojan hero Hector with his H dropped, as the 'ero spelling shows

explanation.surface: A Trojan champion in a hideout comes back, rather as a famous comedian did at a Scottish university.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ero mimics a dropped H, telling you Hector loses his. Stephen Fry was elected rector of the University of Dundee.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Fry was elected rector of Dundee University, so his role there was of that kind.

clue.text: Downcast not downcast?

parts.note: one word for downcast means dejected, but read as two words it is the opposite of 'down' plus a synonym of 'cast'

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words: the opposite of down plus a synonym of cast, so 'not down-cast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dejected or distressed is to be downcast, and the same word splits into the reverse of down plus cast.

clue.text: See 14
The 27's heavy, that's him in France, trapping 100 rebellious Arabs

indicators.note: the French pronoun traps the other letters inside it

parts.note: lui is French for him
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mobster's enforcer, found in France, holds a hundred unruly Arabs captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is The Godfather, so 'The 27's heavy' is that film's enforcer; a heavy is gangster slang for a hired tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Luca Brasi is the Corleone family's hulking enforcer in The Godfather, a heavy in gangster slang.

clue.text: American-Italian exploiter lying about our times

indicators.note: the word for lying goes about the era abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: prone means lying face down
AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A crooked boss of Italian immigrants lies about the modern age.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno domini) stands for our era, here 'our times'.
explanation.definitionFit: A padrone was an Italian-American boss who exploited immigrant labourers in the US.

clue.text: Brokenhearted, wet and I can't be resuscitated

indicators.note: broken letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A heartbroken, tearful person says they are beyond reviving.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Brokenhearted' must be split: its first part is the anagram signal working on the rest along with the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond recovery or revival, like a failed plan, is said to be in that hopeless state.

clue.text: Who's machine? Is dat right? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks, in dialect, whether that is the right gadget, and is told it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who's' is Doctor Who's, not a question; the time machine belongs to the TV Doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor in the BBC series Doctor Who travels in this police-box time machine.

clue.text: Humble traveller in so much of France

parts.note: a rep, sales representative, is a commercial traveller
French en means in and tant means so much

explanation.surface: A modest travelling salesman finds himself in a large part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of France' turns both 'in' and 'so much' into French: EN and TANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being humbled and sorry for one's wrongs, contrite, is the sense shared by the two words.

clue.text: Illuminate with reflection from Sat-Nav aspect

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run backwards
the letters are taken from inside the words Sat-Nav aspect

explanation.surface: A satellite navigation display lights up with reflected light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illuminate' is the noun, one of the enlightened. The run TNAVAS inside 'Sat-Nav aspect', read backwards with 'with reflection', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An illuminate, one claiming special enlightenment, is a learned person or scholar.

clue.text: Mace a sergeant wielded en passant!

indicators.note: wielded letters are swung about into a new order
French for passing, so the letters of en pass out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sergeant swings his club as he goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: Mace is the spray, not the club. 'wielded' rearranges A SERGEANT, and 'en passant' says EN is passed over, so the anagram gives the answer without it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is a trade name for an incapacitating spray, a kind of tear gas.

clue.text: Author-poet singularly 1across 4across 21

parts.note: in the singular, the first word of the linked answer is sleep, kip in slang
in the singular, the final word of the linked answer is fish, and ling is a fish

explanation.surface: A writer is described, singly, by the gangster line from the linked answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singularly' makes each word singular: sleep with the fish, so KIP (sleep) with LING (a fish). 4across, 'with the', is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote both prose fiction and verse, so is fairly an author and poet.

clue.text: Massages the figures with declared deficiencies

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: needs are wants or deficiencies

explanation.surface: A masseur works on bodies that have spoken-for shortcomings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the figures' are the bodies being massaged; 'declared' signals a homophone of NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work muscles with the hands, which is what massaging does.

clue.text: Evans, once keeper of, eg, dry pitches

indicators.note: pitches throws the letters about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former wicketkeeper is said to keep dry cricket pitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitches' looks like cricket grounds, but it is the anagram verb. Godfrey Evans was England's wicketkeeper in the 1940s and 50s.
explanation.definitionFit: Godfrey Evans was a famous England wicketkeeper; his first name is the answer.

clue.text: See 1 across
Travel in time beyond it and back from Rome

indicators.note: the in-time pieces come beyond, after, the first word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: the Latin word is read backwards

parts.note: et is Latin for and, hence 'from Rome'

explanation.surface: Travelling in time past this point and returning from Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Rome' tells you to use Latin: ET for 'and', which 'back' turns to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To itinerate is to travel from place to place, as a circuit preacher or judge did.

clue.text: Girl of the Spanish fiction

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a lie is a fiction, an untruth

explanation.surface: A young woman features in a piece of Spanish fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellie is a common girl's name, as crossword setters often clue a first name.

clue.text: Scotsman rejected commercial spirit with water

indicators.note: the name is thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
ad is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: A Scotsman turns down an advertisement for whisky with water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests whisky and water; the spirit is a water nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a nymph of Greek myth who lives in rivers, springs or lakes.

clue.text: French king rising to embrace Switzerland's divine humour

indicators.note: the turned word embraces the country code, holding it inside
in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: roi is French for king
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A French monarch rises to hug Switzerland, with heavenly good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suits a down clue, where the king's word reads upwards. Switzerland's code comes from its Latin name, Confoederatio Helvetica. Humour is the old sense of a bodily fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor flows in the veins of the gods, a divine fluid as the old bodily humours were.

clue.text: Where one put up with Lawrence during the short vac

indicators.note: Lawrence comes during, within, the holiday

parts.note: a vac is a vacation, a holiday, which shortened is hol
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

explanation.surface: Somewhere a guest stayed with Lawrence over the brief university holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, supplies TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is where travellers are put up, given a room for the night.

clue.text: Family film sponsor

definitions.meaning: the Coppola film about a Mafia family
a man who sponsors a child at baptism

explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Mafia family movie is also the word for a male sponsor at a christening.

clue.text: Cat smooths the way? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the pieces are taken in the reverse of the clue's order

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
evens means smooths or levels

explanation.surface: A cat eases the path, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer Cat Stevens is the reference: 'On the contrary' puts the way before smooths.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer-songwriter Cat Stevens: the answer completes his name after Cat.

clue.text: S-stay behind for such a night with Van Gogh

definitions.text: such a night with Van Gogh

parts.note: the stammered first letter given as written
to tarry is to linger or stay behind

explanation.surface: A stammering invitation to linger on a night like the one Van Gogh painted.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'S-' gives an extra S before the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Gogh's painting The Starry Night makes the answer such a night.
